paragraphs: This report combines the Annual Reports on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 for OneMain Holdings, Inc. ("OMH"), a publicly held financial service holding company, and its wholly-owned direct subsidiary, OneMain Finance Corporation ("OMFC"). OMFC is the issuing entity of our outstanding public debt securities and all of OMFC's common stock is owned by OMH. The information in this combined report is equally applicable to OMH and OMFC, except where otherwise indicated. OMH and OMFC are referred to in this report, collectively with their subsidiaries, whether directly or indirectly owned, as "the Company," "OneMain," "we," "us," or "our."
As one of the nation's leaders in offering nonprime consumers responsible access to credit, we:
•offer personal loan products; •offer secured auto financing at the point of purchase; •offer credit card products;
•offer optional products; •offer a customer-focused financial wellness platform (Trim by OneMain);
•service loans owned by us and third parties; •pursue strategic acquisitions and dispositions of assets and businesses; and
•may establish joint ventures or enter into other strategic alliances.

We provide origination, underwriting, and servicing of consumer loans, consisting of personal loans and auto finance. In addition, we offer BrightWay credit cards through a third-party bank partner from which we purchase the receivable balances. We believe we are well positioned for future growth with an experienced management team, proven access to the capital markets, and strong demand for consumer credit. At December 31, 2025, we had $24.8 billion of finance receivables due from approximately 3.6 million customer accounts. We service the loans that we retain on our balance sheet, as well as loans owned by third parties. At December 31, 2025, we had $26.3 billion of managed receivables due from approximately 3.8 million customer accounts.

Our branch network of more than 1,300 locations is staffed by experienced loan specialists. This network is complemented by our digital lending and servicing capabilities, central operations staff and our network of franchise and independent auto dealerships. Together, these resources allow us to operate in 48 states and serve more customers through their preferred channel: in person, digitally, and over the phone.

We operate in the consumer finance industry serving consumers who typically have more limited access to credit from banks, credit card companies, and other lenders. Using third party market data as of December 2025 and internally aligning to our current product offerings, we estimate U.S. nonprime consumers collectively have approximately $1.3 trillion of outstanding borrowings in the form of personal loans, auto loans and leases, and credit cards. We believe this large market provides us with an attractive growth opportunity.

Our national branch network and digital platform, combined with our central operations and our network of auto dealerships, provide the opportunity for the Company to serve this market efficiently and responsibly. Our auto finance and credit card offerings continue to deepen our existing customer relationships, attract new customers, and further our vision to be the lender of choice for nonprime consumers. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the significant growth and expansion opportunity within our industry. See also "Competition" included in this report.

At December 31, 2025, Consumer and Insurance ("C&I") was our only reportable segment. We originate and service personal loans and auto finance loans, offer credit cards, and provide optional credit and non-credit insurance and other optional products through our branch and central operations, as well as our digital platform. Consumer loan origination and servicing, credit cards, and insurance products form the core of our operations.

Our insurance business is conducted through our wholly-owned insurance subsidiaries, American Health and Life Insurance Company ("AHL") and Triton Insurance Company ("Triton"). AHL is a life and health insurance company licensed in 49 states, the District of Columbia, and Canada to write credit life, credit disability, and non-credit insurance products. Triton is a property and casualty insurance company licensed in 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Canada to write credit involuntary unemployment, credit disability, and collateral protection insurance. See Note 11 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II - Item 8 in this report for further information on our insurance business.

Products and Services. We offer personal loans through our branch network, central operations, digital affiliates, and our website, www.onemainfinancial.com, to consumers who need timely access to cash. Our personal loans are non-revolving, with a fixed rate, have fixed terms generally between three and six years, and are secured by automobiles, other titled collateral, or are unsecured. Our loans have no pre-payment penalties.

Auto finance includes automobile retail installment contracts originated at the point of purchase through a growing network of franchise and independent dealerships. Auto finance loans are non-revolving, with a fixed rate, have fixed terms generally between three and six years, and are secured by automobiles.

We operate in a highly competitive market, and we cannot ensure that the competitive pressures we face will not have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity.

Current and proposed regulations relating to consumer privacy, data protection, and cybersecurity could increase our costs.

Certain of our outstanding notes contain covenants that restrict our operations and may inhibit our ability to grow our business and increase revenues.

OMFC's credit ratings could adversely affect our ability to raise capital in the debt markets at attractive rates, which could negatively affect our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity.

paragraphs: We face a variety of risks that are inherent in our business. In addition to the factors discussed in this report and in other documents we file with the SEC that could adversely affect our businesses, financial condition, and results of operations, new risks may emerge at any time, and we cannot predict those risks or estimate the extent to which they may affect our business or financial performance. Therefore, the risk factors below should not be considered a complete list of potential risks that we may face.

Any risk factor described in this Annual Report on Form 10-K or in any of our other SEC filings could by itself, or together with other factors, materially adversely affect our liquidity, competitive position, business, reputation, results of operations, or financial condition, including by materially increasing our expenses or decreasing our revenues, which could result in material losses.

Our financial condition and results of operations and our borrowers' ability to make payments on their loans have been, and may in the future be, adversely affected by economic conditions and other factors that we cannot control.

Uncertainty and deterioration in general economic conditions in the U.S. and abroad historically have created a difficult operating environment for consumer lending. Many factors, including factors that are beyond our control, may impact our financial condition or results of operations and/or affect our borrowers' willingness or capacity to make payments on their loans. These factors include: unemployment levels, housing markets, energy costs, inflation, and interest rates; events such as natural disasters, acts of war, terrorism, or catastrophes; events that affect our borrowers, such as major medical expenses, divorce, or death; and the quality of any collateral underlying our finance receivables. If we experience a future economic downturn, or if we become affected by other events beyond our control, we may experience increased credit risks, significant reductions in revenues, earnings and cash flows, difficulties accessing capital, and a deterioration in the value of our investments.

Moreover, our customers are primarily nonprime borrowers, who have historically been more likely to be affected, or more severely affected, by adverse macroeconomic conditions than prime borrowers. If a borrower defaults on a finance receivable held directly by us, we will bear a risk of loss of principal to the extent of any deficiency between the value of the collateral, if any, and the outstanding principal and accrued but unpaid interest on the finance receivable, which could adversely affect our cash flows from operations. The cost to service our loans may also increase without a corresponding increase in our finance charge income.

We also are exposed to geographic customer concentration risk. An economic downturn or catastrophic event that disproportionately affects certain geographic regions could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations, including the performance of our finance receivables portfolio. See Note 5 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II - Item 8 in this report for quantification of our largest concentrations of net finance receivables.

We offer consumer loans, which consist of personal loans and auto finance, credit cards, and other products to help customers meet everyday needs and take steps to improve their financial well-being. We service the loans that we retain on our balance sheet, as well as loans owned by third parties. Additionally, our insurance subsidiaries offer optional credit and non-credit insurance and other optional products. We also offer credit cards under our BrightWay brand which are designed to offer a highly digital customer experience while also rewarding customers for responsible credit activity. Our resources allow us to operate in 48 states and provide a seamless experience through our customers' preferred channels, including in person, online or over the phone, using our digital platforms, distribution partnerships, or working with our expert team members at more than 1,300 locations.

•Personal Loans — We offer personal loans through our branch network, central operations, direct mail, digital affiliates, and our website, www.onemainfinancial.com, to customers who need timely access to cash. Our personal loans are non-revolving, with a fixed rate, have fixed terms generally between three and six years, and are secured by automobiles, other titled collateral, or are unsecured. At December 31, 2025, we had approximately 2.4 million personal loans totaling $21.4 billion of net finance receivables, of which 53% were secured by titled property, compared to approximately 2.4 million personal loans totaling $20.8 billion of net finance receivables, of which 50% were secured by titled property at December 31, 2024. We also service personal loans for our whole loan sale partners.

•Auto Finance — We offer secured auto financing originated at the point of purchase through a growing network of franchise and independent dealerships. The loans are non-revolving, with a fixed rate, and have fixed terms generally between three and six years. At December 31, 2025, we had approximately 148 thousand auto finance loans totaling $2.5 billion of net finance receivables, compared to approximately 127 thousand auto finance loans totaling $2.1 billion of net finance receivables at December 31, 2024. We also service auto finance loans for our whole loan sale partners and loans originated by third parties.

•Credit Cards — BrightWay credit cards are originated through a third-party bank partner from which we purchase the receivable balances. The credit cards are offered across our branch network, as well as through direct mail, our digital affiliates, and our website. Credit cards are open-ended, revolving, with a fixed rate, and are unsecured. At December 31, 2025, we had approximately 1.1 million open credit card customer accounts, totaling $936 million of net finance receivables, compared to approximately 783 thousand open credit card customer accounts, totaling $643 million of net finance receivables at December 31, 2024.

•Optional Products — We offer our customers optional credit insurance products (life, disability, and involuntary unemployment insurance) and optional non-credit insurance products through both our branch network and our central operations. Credit insurance and non-credit insurance products are provided by our affiliated insurance companies. We offer Guaranteed Asset Protection ("GAP") coverage as a waiver product or insurance. We also offer optional membership plans from an unaffiliated company.

At December 31, 2025, Consumer and Insurance ("C&I") is our only reportable segment, which includes consumer loans, credit cards, and optional products. At December 31, 2025, we had $26.3 billion of managed receivables due from approximately 3.8 million customer accounts, compared to $24.7 billion of managed receivables due from approximately 3.4 million customer accounts at December 31, 2024.

The remaining components (which we refer to as "Other") consist of our liquidating SpringCastle Portfolio servicing activity and our non-originating legacy operations, which primarily include our liquidating real estate loans held for sale and reported in Other assets in our consolidated balance sheets. See Note 18 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II - Item 8 in this report for more information about our segment.
We closely monitor the primary drivers of pretax operating income, which consist of the following:

We track interest income, including certain fees earned on our finance receivables, and continually monitor the components that impact our yield. We include any late charges on loans that we have collected from customer payments in interest income.

We track the interest expense incurred on our debt to monitor the components of our cost of funds. We expect interest expense to fluctuate based on changes in the secured versus unsecured mix of our debt, time to maturity, interest rates, and utilization of revolving conduit facilities, credit card revolving variable funding note ("VFN") facilities, and the unsecured corporate revolver.

本報告結合 OneMain Holdings, Inc. ("OMH") 以及其 wholly-owned direct subsidiary OneMain Finance Corporation ("OMFC") 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度的 Annual Reports on Form 10-K。OMFC 為本公司發行的公開發行債務證券之發行機構，且 OMFC 全部普通股皆為 OMH 所擁有。本結合報告中之資訊對 OMH 與 OMFC 均適用，除非另有說明。本報告中，OMH 與 OMFC 連同其直接或間接擁有之子公司，統稱為 "the Company," "OneMain," "we," "us," 或 "our."
作為美國在非優質消費者提供負責任信貸存取之領導者之一，我們：
• 提供個人貸款產品；• 提供於購販點提供擔保汽車融資；• 提供信用卡產品；
• 提供選購性產品；• 提供以客戶為中心的財務健康平台 (Trim by OneMain)；
• 服務我們所有及第三方所有之貸款；• 追求戰略收購與資產與業務之處分；以及
• 可能設立合資企業或進行其他戰略聯盟。

我們提供消費者貸款之發行、審核與服務，包含個人貸款與汽車融資。此外，我們透過第三方銀行夥伴提供 BrightWay 信用卡，我們從該銀行夥伴處購買應收款金額。我們相信我們在未來成長方面處於優勢地位，擁有經驗豐富之管理團隊、已驗證之資本市場接觸管道，以及消費者信貸之強勁需求。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們有 248 億美元之應收款金額，來自約 360 萬個客戶帳戶。我們服務我們保留於資產負債表內之貸款，以及第三方所有之貸款。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們有 263 億美元之管理應收款金額，來自約 380 萬個客戶帳戶。
我們擁有超過 1,300 個據點之分行網路，由經驗豐富之貸款專員支援。此網路由我們之數位貸款與服務能力、中央運作人員以及我們之特許與獨立汽車經銷商網路所補強。這些資源使我們得以在 48 個州運作，並透過客戶偏好的通路服務更多客戶：親臨現場、數位化與電話通話。
本公司經營於消費者金融產業，服務的消費者通常較難從銀行、信用卡公司及其他貸款機構取得信貸。根據2025年12月第三方市場資料，並配合本公司目前的產品組合，我們估計美國非優質消費者 collectively 有約1.3兆美元的未償還貸款，形式為個人貸款、汽車貸款與租賃，以及信用卡。我們認為這個龐大市場為本公司提供有吸引力的成長機會。
本公司全國性分行網路與數位平台，結閤中央運作及汽車經銷商網路，為本公司服務此市場提供高效且負責任的機會。本公司汽車金融與信用卡產品持續深化現有客戶關係，吸引新客戶，並進一步實現本公司成為非優質消費者首選貸款機構的願景。我們認為本公司已具備良好的條件，可把握產業內顯著的成長與擴張機會。請參閱本報告中「競爭」部分。
2025年12月31日，消費者與保險（"C&I"）為本公司唯一應報告分部。我們透過分行與中央運作，以及數位平台，發放並服務個人貸款與汽車金融貸款，提供信用卡，並透過分行與中央運作，以及數位平台，提供選擇性信貸與非信貸保險及其他選擇性產品。個人貸款發放與服務、信用卡與保險產品為本公司營運的核心。

本公司保險業務透過本公司百分之百持股的保險子公司，美國健康與人壽保險公司（"AHL"）與特里通保險公司（"Triton"）進行。AHL 是一家在49個州、華盛頓特區與加拿大持有牌照的壽險與健康險公司，可提供信貸壽險、信貸失能險與非信貸保險產品。Trit, 是一家在50個州、華盛頓特區與加拿大持有牌照的財產與意外險公司，可提供信貸非自願失業險、信貸失能險與擔保保護險。請參閱本報告第二部分-第8項「綜合財務報表附註」中的第11項附註，以取得更多關於本公司保險業務的資訊。
產品與服務。本公司透過分行網路、中央運作、數位加盟夥伴及網站www.onemainfinancial.com，為需要即時現金的消費者提供個人貸款。本公司個人貸款為非循環貸款，利率固定，貸款期限通常為3至6年，並以汽車、其他有標題的擔保品或無擔保為抵押。本公司貸款無預先償還罰款。
汽車金融包括於購車時點透過不斷擴張的連鎖與獨立經銷商網路所發行的汽車零售 installment 合約。汽車金融貸款為非循環貸款，利率固定，貸款期限通常為3至6年，並以汽車為抵押。

我們提供消費者貸款，包括個人貸款與汽車融資、信用卡及其他產品，以協助客戶滿足日常需求並採取行動改善其財務狀況。我們服務我們保留於資產負債表上的貸款，以及由第三方持有的貸款。此外，我們的保險子公司提供選擇性信用與非信用保險及其他選擇性產品。我們也透過 BrightWay 品牌提供信用卡，這些信用卡設計為提供高度數位化的客戶體驗，同時也獎勵客戶負責任的信用活動。我們的資源使我們能在 48 個州運作，並透過客戶偏好的通路提供順暢的體驗，包括親臨現場、線上或電話，使用我們的數位平台、分銷合作夥伴，或與我們在超過 1,300 個據點的專業團隊成員合作。

•個人貸款 — 我們透過我們的分行網路、中央運營、直郵、數位合作夥伴及我們的網站 www.onemainfinancial.com，為需要即時現金的客戶提供個人貸款。我們的個人貸款為非循環貸款，利率固定，貸款期限通常為三至六年，並以汽車、其他有標題的擔保品或無擔保方式提供。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約有 240 萬筆個人貸款，總計淨融資應收款為 214 億美元，其中 53% 以有標題的財產擔保，與截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日約有 240 萬筆個人貸款，總計淨融資應收款為 208 億美元，其中 50% 以有標題的財產擔保的情況相比。我們也為我們的整筆貸款銷售合作夥伴服務個人貸款。

•汽車融資 — 我們透過不斷擴張的特許與獨立經銷商網路，在購車時點提供有擔保的汽車融資。貸款為非循環貸款，利率固定，貸款期限通常為三至六年。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約有 148,000 筆汽車融資貸款，總計淨融資應收款為 25 億美元，與截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日約有 127,000 筆汽車融資貸款，總計淨融資應收款為 21 億美元的情況相比。我們也為我們的整筆貸款銷售合作夥伴及由第三方發行的貸款服務汽車融資貸款。

•信用卡 — BrightWay 信用卡是由第三方銀行夥伴發行，我們從該銀行夥伴處購買應收帳款餘額。信用卡透過我們的分行網路、直郵、數位 affiliates 以及網站提供。信用卡為無限額循環信貸，固定利率，且為無擔保貸款。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約有 1.1 百萬筆開放式信用卡客戶帳戶，總計 936 百萬美元的淨金融應收款，相較於 2024 年 12 月 31 日約有 783 千筆開放式信用卡客戶帳戶，總計 643 百萬美元的淨金融應收款。
•選擇性產品 — 我們為客戶提供選擇性信用保險產品（包括壽險、殘疾保險及非自願失業保險）與選擇性非信用保險產品，透過我們的分行網路與中央作業中心提供。信用保險與非信用保險產品由我們的附屬保險公司提供。我們也提供保證資產保護（"GAP"）覆蓋作為免責產品或保險。我們也提供來自無關聯公司的選擇性會員計畫。

{'At December 31, 2025, Consumer and Insurance ("C&I") is our only reportable segment, which includes consumer loans, credit cards, and optional products.': '於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，消費者及保險（"C&I"）為本公司唯一應報告分部，包含消費者貸款、信用卡及選擇性產品。', 'At December 31, 2025, we had $26.3 billion of managed receivables due from approximately 3.8 million customer accounts, compared to $24.7 billion of managed receivables due from approximately 3.4 million customer accounts at December 31, 2024.': '於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司有 26.3 十億美元的應收帳款，來自約 3.8 千萬客戶帳戶，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 24.7 十億美元應收帳款，來自約 3.4 千萬客戶帳戶相比。'}
其餘零組件（我們稱為"其他"）包含我們正在清算的SpringCastle Portfolio的服務活動與我們非發起的遺留作業，主要包含我們正在清算的房地產貸款，持有待售，並在我們合併財務報表的其他資產中報告。請參閱本報告第二部分第8項「重要會計政策」中第18節的說明，以取得更多關於我們分部的資訊。
我們密切監測預稅營運收入的主要驅動因素，這些因素包含以下內容：
我們追蹤利息收入，包括我們財務應收款上所收取的某些費用，並持續監測影響我們收益率的零組件。我們將任何已從客戶付款中收取的貸款違約費用納入利息收入。
我們追蹤我們債務所產生的利息支出，以監測我們資金成本的零組件。我們預期利息支出將根據我們債務中擔保與無擔保組成比例的變化、到期時間、利率以及循環融資設施的使用情況、信用卡循環變動資金貸款（"VFN"）設施以及無擔保企業循環貸款的使用情況而有所波動。

headings: 若本公司對融資應收款損失之撥備之估計不足以吸收實際損失，則融資應收款損失之撥備將增加，可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司風險管理措施可能無法達到預期效果。
本公司業務及聲譽可能因資訊系統故障、網路攻擊或網路中斷而受到重大影響。
本公司亦可能因設施內客戶及員工之實體記錄遭竊取或濫用而受到影響。
本公司保險業務面臨風險與不確定性，包括賠償聲請、重大災害事件、承保風險及對主要分銷渠道之依賴。
本公司使用衍生性金融商品，將面臨信用及市場風險。
本公司可能無法如部分競爭對手般迅速進行技術改良，這可能影響本公司競爭能力，並對財務狀況、營運成果及流動性造成不利影響。
若商譽及其他無形資產發生減值，將對本公司獲利能力產生負面影響。
對本公司聲譽的損害可能會對本公司業務及財務結果產生不利影響。
本公司營運於高度競爭的市場，本公司無法確保所面對的競爭壓力不會對本公司財務狀況、營運結果及流動性產生重大不利影響。
杜克·弗蘭克法案的規範要求及消費者金融保護局的監督大幅增加本公司的監管成本與負擔。
現行及擬議的消費者隱私權、資料保護及網路安全相關規範可能會增加本公司的成本。
本公司使用第三方供應商的作法將受到監管審查。
法律的變更及監管發展可能會導致與資產證券化相關的重大額外合規成本。
本公司可能必須限制業務活動以避免被視為投資公司於投資公司法案下。
無法取得足夠的流動性來源可能會對本公司履行營運需求及財務義務的能力產生不利影響。
本公司部分尚未償還的票據包含約束我們營運的條款，可能抑制我們擴大業務與增加營業收入的能力。
本公司流動性的評估基於重大判斷與估計，這些判斷與估計可能產生重大錯誤。
OMFC 的信用評級可能影響本公司在債務市場以有吸引力的利率籌資的能力，這可能會對本公司的財務狀況、營運成果與流動性產生負面影響。
本公司的資產證券化可能使我們面臨融資及其他風險，且無法保證我們未來能夠進入證券化市場，這可能需要我們尋求成本更高的融資。
OMH 與 OMFC 為控股公司，無實際營運，並依賴本公司的營運子公司提供資金以履行財務義務並支付股息。
即使達成流動性與負債目標，OMH 未來可能不會支付其普通股股息。
本公司重組後的公司章程與修正後的章程條款可能阻礙、延宕或防止 OMH 的控制權變更，這可能會對 OMH 普通股的價格產生負面影響。
授權與保險法規可能延宕或阻礙購買 OMH 普通股。
paragraphs: 我們面臨許多與業務本質相關的風險。除了本報告及我們向 SEC 提交的其他文件中提及的可能對我們業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響的因素外，任何時間都可能出現新的風險，我們無法預測這些風險或估計它們可能對我們業務或財務表現產生的影響。因此，下列風險因素不應被視為我們可能面臨的全部潛在風險清單。
本年度10-K表報表或我們其他SEC申報文件中所描述的任何風險因素，單獨或與其他因素共同作用，都可能對我們的流動性、競爭地位、業務、聲譽、營運成果或財務狀況產生重大不利影響，包括可能顯著增加我們的費用或減少我們的營業收入，這可能會導致重大虧損。
我們的財務狀況及營運成果，以及借款人償還貸款的能力，已受到且可能在未來繼續受到我們無法控制的經濟條件及其他因素的不利影響。

美國及國際間的總體經濟狀況的不確定性與惡化，歷來已為消費者貸款業務創造了困難的營運環境。許多因素，包括我們無法控制的因素，可能影響我們的財務狀況或營運成果，並/或影響借款人償還貸款的意願或能力。這些因素包括：失業率、房地產市場、能源成本、通貨膨脹及利率；如天然災害、戰爭行為、恐怖主義或災難等事件；影響借款人的事件，如重大醫療支出、離婚或死亡；以及任何擔保品的品質。如果我們遭遇未來經濟衰退，或受到其他我們無法控制的事件影響，我們可能會面臨增加的信用風險、營收顯著減少、獲利與現金流下降，以及難以取得資金，並導致我們投資價值的惡化。
此外，我們的客戶主要是非優質借款人，這些借款人歷來較容易受到或更嚴重地受到不利總體經濟條件的影響，與優質借款人相比。如果借款人未能償還我們直接持有的貸款，我們將承擔本金損失的風險，範圍為擔保品價值（如有）與貸款本金及應計未付利息之間的差額，這可能會對我們的營運現金流產生不利影響。我們貸款的服務成本也可能增加，而我們的貸款利息收入卻未必同步增加。
我們也面臨地理上客戶集中風險。若某些地理區域受到經濟衰退或災難性事件的 disproportionately 影響，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利的影響，包括我們貸款組合的表現。請參閱本報告第二部分-第8項「財務會計摘要」中第5項附註，以取得我們最大淨貸款組合集中度的量化資訊。
